profile_text.body:
The Technology Innovation Institute is a non-profit government research laboratory founded in 2020, described on its site as the applied research pillar of Abu Dhabi's Advanced Technology Research Council (ATRC). It presents itself as a global scientific research center and develops the Falcon family of generative large language models, which it describes as open-source, multilingual, and multimodal.

The Falcon line includes Falcon 180B, a 180 billion parameter model trained on 3.5 trillion tokens; Falcon 40B, trained on 40 billion parameters and one trillion tokens and described as the first home-grown open source LLM released with weights for research and commercial use; Falcon Mamba 7B, described as the first open source State Space Language Model; Falcon 2 11B; Falcon-H1 and Falcon-E; Falcon Arabic, aimed at Modern Standard Arabic and dialects; Falcon Perception, a multimodal model for reading and understanding images from natural language prompts; and Falcon H1R 7B, a 7B reasoning model. The site states that Falcon-H1 uses a hybrid Transformer and Mamba architecture and that Falcon 2 11B outperforms Meta's Llama 3 8B and performs on par with Google's Gemma 7B, as verified on the Hugging Face Leaderboard. The institute also announced the launch of the Falcon Foundation, a non-profit dedicated to open-source generative AI models, and Falcon 10B has been the subject of a Call for Proposals by AI71, a company launched by ATRC and VentureOne, and of a hackfest run by the institute.

The available record lists Falcon (TII) as an open-source, Apache 2.0 licensed model hosted in the UAE, with Middle East data residency and sovereign AI positioning. No lawsuits or MCP servers are recorded for the company.
